All three variants are live. Each one shows the **same** already-saved bookmark (I pre-loaded the NASA link you saved earlier, so you can focus purely on the tagging feel), and each has an identical **Note** box below. The *only* difference between them is how you add tags.

---

### 👉 Please try each one, in order

**Variant 1 — http://maker:4001/tag-a.html**
In the Tags field, type `space` and press **Enter**. Then type `reading` and press **Enter** again. Notice how each becomes a little removable pill as you go.

**Variant 2 — http://maker:4001/tag-b.html**
In the Tags field, type `space, reading, science` all in one go, separated by commas. Watch the pills form as you type.

**Variant 3 — http://maker:4001/tag-c.html**
Click one of the suggested tags underneath the field (these mimic tags you'd have used before), then type a brand-new word and press Enter to create one that didn't exist yet.

In **any** of them, you can also type something in the **Note** box and click outside it to see the note kept.

---

Two things I decided, please check them too:
- I **pre-loaded one saved bookmark** in each variant just so there's something to tag — that's a prototype convenience, not a new behaviour.
- Tags appear as small removable **pills**; a note is free-form text.

**Which of the three ways of adding tags feels most natural to you** — 1, 2, or 3? And does being able to attach your own tags and a note to a bookmark match what you wanted? If you're unsure between two, tell me which and I'll help you compare.
